basis: Three genuinely different structures share this host and the seed names two of them. InTe and In0.995Te (7 samples) are the TlSe-type mixed-valence In(I)In(III)Te2 chain compound -- MP InTe I4/mcm (140) mp-20320, 9 ICSD refs -- and the lone-pair rattler paper is about exactly that. In4Te3 (4 samples) is the In4Se3-type 4-3 phase, TEDesignLab Pnnm (58) mp-617281 with 9 ICSD refs. In2Te3 and In2(Te0.94Se0.06)3 (6 samples) are the defect-zincblende sesquitelluride, MP F-43m (216) mp-622511, which belongs to sphalerite and is a third prototype the seed does not mention. Against ref 2: it ranks InTe Fm-3m mp-2597 first on 10 ICSD references, but rocksalt InTe is the high-pressure phase, so the ambient assignment stays TlSe-type and the rocksalt goes in other_polymorphs -- the 4 film samples are where it could plausibly appear.

other_polymorphs.note: MP marks InTe Fm-3m PRIMARY on 10 ICSD refs against 9 for I4/mcm, but the rocksalt form is reached by pressure (~3 GPa) or epitaxy, not by heating InTe at ambient pressure. Recorded as a disagreement with the reference rather than followed.

dopant_roles.basis: In2(Te0.94Se0.06)3 and In4Se0.2Te2.8 sit on the In-Se-Te anion solid-solution line -- the In4Se3/In4Te3 and In2Se3/In2Te3 series are continuous, so this is site alloying rather than dilute doping.
Cation site; Cu+ on the In+ site of the TlSe-type structure is the likely target.
Monovalent acceptor on the cation site.

basis: Mo3Sb7 is 9 of the 24 samples outright and every other composition is a substituted Mo3-xMxSb7 or Mo3Sb7-xTex, i.e. the Ir3Ge7-type cubic antimonide: MP Sb7Mo3 Im-3m (229) mp-1521, hull 0.000, 10 ICSD refs, and the only other MP entry (Sb3Mo Fm-3m at hull 0.613) is not a real phase. Worth flagging for stage 2 even though the chunk file does not: Mo3Sb7 undergoes a cubic-to-tetragonal spin-gap distortion near 53 K, inside the 12-993 K window, but it distorts the same Ir3Ge7 framework rather than changing prototype, so it is noted here instead of being split into phases.

dopant_roles.basis: Mo2.6Fe0.4Sb7 -- Fe on the Mo site is the p-type carrier knob in the high-power-factor paper.
Ni0.25Mo2.75...Sb7, heavy Ni doping on the Mo site.
Same-group 4d substituent on the Mo site.
Mo3Sb7-xTex: Te on the Sb site is the electron-count variable that opens the gap.
One composition; iodine in an antimonide synthesis is normally a transport agent or flux residue rather than a lattice substituent.

basis: Every composition is Sr1-xLaxSnO3 (x = 0.01-0.05) plus one (Ba,Sr)SnO3 and one undoped SrSnO3 -- the ABO3 stannate perovskite, orthorhombically tilted: TEDesignLab gives SrSnO3 Pnma (62) mp-2879, hull 0.000, 14 ICSD refs, and one paper calls it perovskite-type in its title. TEDesignLab's other entries for this chemistry are the Sr2SnO4 and Sr3Sn2O7 Ruddlesden-Popper members (7 and 1 ICSD refs), but no composition here has Sr:Sn above 1:1, so they describe the chemistry rather than these samples; ref 2's Sr3SnO antiperovskite is likewise not a candidate.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr1-xLaxSnO3: La3+ for Sr2+ on the A site is the n-type donor and the carrier-concentration variable throughout the host.
Trivalent rare earth on the A site, same donor role as La.
(Ba0.2Sr0.8)0.95La0.05SnO3 is a point on the BaSnO3-SrSnO3 solid solution -- an isovalent end member that happens to fall below 5 at.%, not a dopant.

basis: This host straddles a structural boundary rather than holding one prototype. The Te-rich half (SnTe0.75Se0.25, SnTe0.90Se0.10 -- 8 samples) is cubic rocksalt SnTe with Se on the anion site. The Se-rich half (SnSe0.8Te0.2, SnSe0.88Te0.12 and the Na-doped SnSe1-xTex of the first paper) is orthorhombic Pnma SnSe, i.e. layered_ges: in SnSe1-xTex the Pnma structure survives to roughly x = 0.3-0.4 Te before going cubic, so the crossover sits inside the measured Se/(Se+Te) = 0.10-0.92 range and the split has to be per composition. I take rocksalt at host level because the Te-rich compositions carry the most samples, and flag that the Se-rich branch additionally approaches the SnSe Pnma-to-Cmcm transition near the top of the 826 K window. Ref 2 offers only computed Sn-Se-Te orderings (Sn3Te2Se P-3m1, Sn4Te3Se R3m) with no ICSD backing, none of which is either end member, so it does not settle anything here.

solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) spans 0.10-0.92 with a median of 0.76. Unusually for an isoelectronic axis, the prototype itself changes along it -- rocksalt on the Te-rich side, Pnma layered_ges on the Se-rich side -- so stage 3 must assign the parent from the composition and not from the host.

Se/Cd codoped SnTe: Cd on the cation site both dopes and converges the valence bands.
Monovalent acceptor on the Sn site.

basis: 15 of 23 samples are plain AlN and the rest are AlN with mole-percent Y2O3, CaO or TbN additions -- i.e. wurtzite 2H AlN, which TEDesignLab gives as P6_3mc (186) mp-661, hull 0.000, with 24 ICSD references against 8 for zincblende and 6 for rocksalt. The papers are thermal-conductivity studies of AlN ceramics and substrates, where the additions are densification aids that end up in grain-boundary phases rather than changing the host structure. Zincblende and rocksalt AlN are real but not thermally reached, so they go in other_polymorphs.

other_polymorphs.note: Cubic zincblende AlN, 8 ICSD refs at hull 0.021, is stabilised epitaxially on cubic substrates; bulk ceramic AlN does not convert to it on heating.
Rocksalt AlN appears above roughly 20 GPa (hull 0.172); irrelevant to these ambient-pressure ceramics.

dopant_roles.basis: (Y2O3)1.98(AlN)98.02 -- Y2O3 is a sintering aid that reacts with surface alumina into yttrium-aluminate grain-boundary phases; Y3+ is far too large for the Al site.
(AlN)98.53(CaO)1.47 -- CaO is a sintering aid forming calcium-aluminate grain-boundary phases; the paper is about its effect on thermal conductivity.
(TbN)0.5(AlN)99.5 and (Tb)0.5(AlN)99.5 -- a rare-earth nitride addition, again a grain-boundary oxygen getter rather than a substituent.

Oxygen is the one addition that does enter the AlN lattice: O on the N site with compensating Al vacancies is the accepted mechanism by which oxygen content controls AlN thermal conductivity, which is what these papers measure. Part of it also sits in grain-boundary oxide.

basis: All 12 visible compositions are Bi2V1-xMxO5.5 with M = Cr, Mo or W -- the BIMEVOX family, which is the gamma-Bi4V2O11 Aurivillius structure: Bi2O2 fluorite-like layers alternating with oxygen-deficient perovskite VO3.5 blocks. The taxonomy's aurivillius entry names Bi2VO5.5 as its exemplar, so that half of the seed is confirmed. The other half is wrong and the seed missed the phase that replaces it: no composition here is V2O5, so v2o5_layered is rejected, but two of the three papers are hollandite studies (Bi1.7V8O16, whose Bi fraction of 6.6 at.% puts it in this host), so the remaining compositions are almost certainly BixV8O16 hollandite. Ref 2 supports neither: its best-attested entry is the scheelite orthovanadate VBiO4 I4_1/a mp-25122 (3 ICSD refs), a 1:1:4 stoichiometry absent from this host, and the 2019 dump has no Bi2VO5.5 at all.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi2V1-xCrxO5.5 (BICRVOX): substitution on the V site of the perovskite block, which is what the first paper varies; it also sets the oxygen-vacancy content.
Bi2V1-xMoxO5.5 (BIMOVOX), same V site.
Bi2V1-xWxO5.5 (BIWVOX), same V site.

basis: Every composition is (Ti,Hf)CoSb with Sn on the Sb site -- the 18-electron MgAgAs-type half-Heusler, and two of the three papers say half-Heusler or TiCoSb-ZrCoSb-HfCoSb in their titles. Ti and Hf share the group-IV site so the alloying does not change the prototype, only the mass fluctuation the papers are after. Neither reference covers this host at all, so the call rests on composition plus the papers. One detail for stage 2: Ti0.5Hf0.5Co1.04Sb0.9Sn0.1 carries excess Co, which in this family means Co on the vacant fourth site, i.e. incipient full-Heusler inclusions rather than a different host structure.

solid_solution_axis.note: Hf/(Hf+Ti) spans 0.20-0.50 over 15 compositions; both ends are the same prototype, so the axis matters for mass disorder and lattice thermal conductivity, not for the structure.

dopant_roles.basis: Sb0.85Sn0.15 in most compositions: Sn for Sb removes one electron per substitution and is the p-type carrier-concentration variable.
Pentavalent donor on the group-IV site.
Ti0.6Hf0.4Co0.87Ni0.13Sb -- Ni on the Co site adds electrons and is the n-type knob in this family.
Ti0.75(Zr0.25Hf0.75)0.25CoSb: Zr is a third member of the same group-IV site, part of the (Ti,Zr,Hf) alloy rather than a dopant.

basis: The host is PrCoO3 and Pr0.9A0.1CoO3 with A = Ca, Sr or Ba, plus one B-site Ni substitution -- an ABO3 cobaltite perovskite. MP agrees and picks the right variant: PrCoO3 Pnma (62) mp-24849 at hull 0.000 with 7 ICSD references, the orthorhombically tilted form, against 1 reference for the Pm-3m aristotype. The Pr2CoO4 I4/mmm entry is a Ruddlesden-Popper stoichiometry that no composition here approaches. The 11-1169 K window crosses the thermally driven spin-state and insulator-metal crossovers of Co3+, which change transport sharply but leave the perovskite framework intact, so no phase split is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: Pr0.9Ca0.1CoO3: divalent on the trivalent A site, the hole-doping variable; the third paper is a study of R1-xAxCoO3 across A = Ca, Sr, Ba.
Pr0.9Sr0.1CoO3 and Pr0.8Sr0.2CoO3 -- same A-site hole doping, larger cation.
Pr0.9Ba0.1CoO3 -- A site; the ionic-size paper is about exactly this series.
PrCo0.95Ni0.05O3, B site -- the Ln(Co,Ni)O3 paper.
B-site transition metal.

basis: The entire host is CuRh1-xMgxO2 -- the curator wrote that formula out -- and one paper calls it delafossite oxide in its title, so the 1:1:2 ABO2 layering of O-Cu-O dumbbells between RhO2 sheets is not in doubt; MP has CuRhO2 R-3m (166) mp-14116 at hull 0.000. I am not following ref 2's ranking: it marks Cu(RhO2)2 Fd-3m mp-4409 PRIMARY on 4 ICSD references, but that is spinel CuRh2O4 at Cu:Rh = 1:2, and no composition in this host has more than one Rh per Cu. The single ICSD reference behind CuRhO2 is a snapshot artefact, not evidence against it.

dopant_roles.basis: CuRh1-xMgxO2 with x = 0.01-0.10: Mg2+ for Rh3+ in the octahedral layer is the acceptor and the only doping variable in this host.

basis: Cu2.2V4O11 and Cu2.36V4O11 (10 of 23 samples, and the two single-crystal papers) are the beta'-CuxV4O11 mixed-valence bronze, which the taxonomy's vanadium_bronze entry names this host under -- confirmed for those. The rest of the host is not a bronze: Cu2V2O7 and the Zn0.25-0.5Cu1.75-1.5V2O7 series (4 compositions, the first paper) are stoichiometric V5+ divanadates of the thortveitite-derived ziesite/blossite type, MP V2Cu2O7 C2/c mp-607934 at hull 0.002 with 3 ICSD references. That family had no taxonomy entry, so cu2v2o7_pyrovanadate was proposed for it before use and the host splits on the Cu:V ratio (1:2 bronze versus 1:1 pyrovanadate). MP's other entries here (VCuO3 Im-3, KV3Cu5O13) match no composition present.

dopant_roles.basis: Zn0.25Cu1.75V2O7 to Zn0.5Cu1.5V2O7 is a ZnxCu2-xV2O7 substitutional series on the divanadate cation site (isostructural end members), not dilute doping -- it is the variable the first paper's phase-transition study scans.

basis: Cu2Te and the Cu-deficient Cu1.75Te / Cu1.99Ga0.01Te (10 samples) are the copper chalcogenide superionic family the seed names, and the Ag-doped Cu2Se-and-Cu2Te paper treats them together. Two other prototypes are present, though: Cu27.5Ge2.5Te70 and Cu22.5Ge2.5Te75 come from the conducting-glasses paper on the Cu-Ge-Te system and are not crystalline at all (metallic_glass), and CuIn0.09Zn0.01Te2 belongs to the CuInTe2 chalcopyrite study. On the transition: the chunk file applies the taxonomy default of ~400 K, which is the Cu2Se/Cu2S value and does not transfer -- Cu2Te's order-disorder sequence runs higher, with the ordered superstructure giving way to the disordered hexagonal subcell (MP Cu2Te P6/mmm mp-1861, 4 ICSD refs) in the 500-600 K region. I have recorded ~570 K from materials knowledge, flagged low confidence, and left the low-temperature superstructure's mp_id null rather than pointing it at the subcell entry. MP's primary for this chemistry, CuTe Pmmn mp-20826 (vulcanite, 5 refs), is the 1:1 compound and is not what these compositions are.

Cu1.99Ga0.01Te -- trivalent donor on the Cu site.
CuIn0.09Zn0.01Te2 comes from the CuInTe2 solid-solution paper, so In here is a chalcopyrite constituent, not a Cu2Te dopant.
Same CuInTe2-derived composition, where Zn sits on the group-III site.
Cu2Se and Cu2Te form a continuous anion solid solution, so Se on the Te site is site alloying rather than doping.
Present in 5 compositions but no visible formula shows where it sits; Fe is a poor fit for the Cu site and could be a second phase. Needs the paper.

basis: IrSb3 (5 samples) is the binary skutterudite -- MP Sb3Ir Im-3 (204) mp-1239, hull 0.000, 4 ICSD refs -- and La0.1-0.3Ir4Sb12 and Ba0.3Ir4Sb12 (9 samples) are the same CoAs3 framework with a guest in the icosahedral void, so filled_skutterudite is the second prototype and the split is by whether a filler is present. The seed missed a third: Ir0.9Co0.1Sb2 is the 1:2 diantimonide, which MP gives as Sb2Ir P2_1/c (14) mp-1247 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD refs -- the monoclinic arsenopyrite-type ordering of the marcasite family, not a skutterudite. Split by the Sb:Ir ratio (3 versus 2).

Ba0.3Ir4Sb12, same void.
Alkaline-earth filler, as for Ba.
Alkali filler in the void.
Alkali filler in the void.
La0.1Ir4Ge0.3Sb11.7 -- Ge replaces framework Sb, which is how the electron count is balanced against the La filler rather than a dilute impurity.
IrxCo1-xSb2 and IrxCo1-xSb3 alloys: Co and Ir are fully miscible on the transition-metal site.

basis: All 23 samples are stoichiometric ZrN, the B1 rocksalt nitride: MP ZrN Fm-3m (225) mp-1352, hull 0.000, 37 ICSD references, and the papers are ZrN/ZrC/ZrCN ceramic and nuclear-fuel characterisations. B1 ZrN is stable from low temperature to the melt, so the unusually wide 294-2311 K window crosses no transition. Note against ref 1: TEDesignLab covers this chemistry only through Zr3N4 (Pnma mp-277 and I-43d mp-11661), a nitrogen-rich phase that no sample here is -- the thermoelectric-specific reference simply lacks the ambient compound, exactly the case the chunk header warns about, and ref 2 supplies it instead.

The host is yttria-stabilised zirconia at 8-16 mol% Y2O3, written both as (ZrO2)0.92(Y2O3)0.08 and as Zr0.85Y0.15O1.925, and the first paper is titled 'Thermoelectric power of YSZ'. That composition range is the cubic fluorite field: Y3+ on the Zr site with charge-compensating oxygen vacancies, which is what makes YSZ an electrolyte and gives the glass-like thermal conductivity of the third paper. The 7YSZ coating sample is the metastable tetragonal t' variant used in thermal-barrier coatings, a distortion of the same fluorite prototype rather than a different one, and the Al2O3 bond coat the curator notes is a separate layer, not part of the host. Both references point elsewhere and I am not following them: TEDesignLab lists Y2Zr2O7 (227) and MP the ordered Y4Zr3O12 delta-phase and Y2Zr9O22, all at Y:Zr ratios far above 8 mol% -- phases that exist in the Y-Zr-O system, not the composition measured here.

dopant_roles.basis: (Ta2O5)5.4(Y2O3)9(ZrO2)85.6 -- Ta5+ on the Zr site of a thermal-barrier composition, co-doped with Y to balance the vacancy count.
Same role as Ta, pentavalent on the Zr site.
Trivalent on the Zr site like Y, though La3+ is large enough that a La2Zr2O7 pyrochlore second phase is possible at higher levels.

basis: 10 of 23 samples are plain InAs and the rest are Be-, Ga- or Mn-doped InAs -- zincblende III-V, MP InAs F-43m (216) mp-20305 at hull 0.000 with 25 ICSD references, an order of magnitude more than any other polymorph. The wurtzite and rocksalt entries are real but not thermally reached from bulk zincblende, so they sit in other_polymorphs; the 7 film and epitaxial samples are where wurtzite could genuinely appear, which is why it is recorded rather than dropped.

2 ICSD refs at hull 0.197; the pressure-induced B1 phase, not on any heating path.

In1-xGaxAs is a continuous isovalent alloy on the group-III site; the second paper studies In1-xGaxAs crystals.
Group-V anion alloying (InAsP), same continuum.
Mn on the group-III site, the dilute-magnetic-semiconductor substitution.

basis: 19 of 22 samples are CeB6 single crystals and the other three are Ce1-xLaxB6 -- the CaB6 cubic hexaboride with B6 octahedra and Ce in the cube centres. MP CeB6 Pm-3m (221) mp-21343 sits at hull 0.000 with 26 ICSD references; the only other entry, CeB4 P4/mbm with 4 refs, is the tetraboride and no composition here is 1:4. The papers are Kondo-lattice and heavy-fermion transport studies across 10-303 K, where CeB6's antiferroquadrupolar and antiferromagnetic orderings occur without changing the crystal prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce1-xLaxB6 at x = 0.03-0.25: trivalent 4f-empty La on the Ce site dilutes the Kondo lattice rather than doping carriers, which is exactly what the thermopower papers vary.

basis: Every composition is Ba0.5Sr0.5Co1-yFeyO3-delta with y = 0.3-0.6 -- BSCF, the cubic ABO3 perovskite with Ba/Sr disordered on the A site and Co/Fe on the B site, and the papers are SOFC-cathode assessments of exactly that series. Ref 2 gives no usable evidence either way: all four entries are computed BaSr7Fe6-7Co1-2O20-24 supercells with no ICSD backing, which are orderings of the same perovskite rather than alternative structures. At the Co content used here the vacancies stay disordered, so this is a perovskite and not the brownmillerite that Fe-rich SrFeO2.5 forms; the delta in O3-delta is the oxygen non-stoichiometry, not an impurity. One thing for stage 2: BSCF is known to degrade towards hexagonal and ordered phases after long exposure above roughly 1100 K, inside this 374-1239 K window, so the papers should be checked for that.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba0.5Sr0.5Co0.7Fe0.28La0.02O3 -- both the formula and the paper title ('B-site La, Ce, and Pr-doped') put La on the B site, which is unusual for a large rare earth and worth confirming in stage 2.
Same series, B site per the formula and paper title.
Same series, B site per the formula and paper title.
B-site transition metal.
B-site substituent on the octahedral site.

basis: The host is DyBa2Cu3O7 and Dy0.95Pr0.05Ba2(Cu0.98M0.02)3O7 -- the RBa2Cu3O7-delta 123 structure with Dy on the Y site, and both papers are titled for RBa2Cu3O7 normal-state transport. MP has Ba2DyCu3O7 Pmmm (47) mp-622105, the orthorhombic 123 cell. I am not taking ref 2's ranking at face value: it marks Ba2Dy(CuO2)4 Cmmm mp-6691 PRIMARY on 3 ICSD references, but that is the 124 double-chain polytype, and BaDy2CuO5 is the insulating green phase -- both exist in this chemistry while every composition here is 1:2:3. The 10-301 K window contains the superconducting transition, which is electronic and leaves the structure alone.

dopant_roles.basis: Dy0.95Pr0.05Ba2Cu3O7 -- Pr on the rare-earth site is the classic hole-localising substitution in 123 cuprates, present in 15 of 22 samples.
(Cu0.98Fe0.02)3: Fe substitutes on the CuO chain site preferentially, the subject of the third paper's M-series.
Same M-series; Co also prefers the chain site.
Same M-series; Ni prefers the CuO2 plane site.
Same M-series; Zn is the canonical in-plane Cu substituent.

basis: 14 of the 20 compositions are Ba3Cu14-dTe12 with the Cu deficiency scanned from Ba3Cu13.175Te12 to Ba3Cu13.975Te12, which is the polytelluride reported in the first paper ('the New Polytelluride Ba3Cu14-dTe12'); BaCu2Te2 (2 samples) is a separate 1:2:2 line compound, MP Ba(CuTe)2 Pnma (62) mp-30133 at hull 0.014. Neither phase had a taxonomy entry -- this host was unassignable as it stood -- so ba3cu14te12_polytelluride and bacu2s2_layered were both proposed before use and the host splits on the Ba:Cu ratio. The references are thin: TEDesignLab's only entry is Ba6NaCu3Te14 (193), a sodium-containing phase absent from this host, and MP's single entry rests on one ICSD reference. The Cu deficiency d is the carrier-concentration variable, not an impurity.

dopant_roles.basis: Same-group monovalent cation on the partially occupied Cu framework sites.
Anion-site alloying in a chalcogenide framework rather than dilute doping.

basis: Every composition is Hg1-xCdxSe with x = 0.21-0.35 carrying 0.03-3 at.% of a 3d impurity, all from one paper on Fe, Co and Cr impurities in that alloy. HgSe is zincblende and the alloy stays in the cubic tetrahedral net at these Cd levels, so sphalerite covers the whole host -- worth noting that pure CdSe is wurtzite, so the prototype would change somewhere well above the x = 0.35 reached here. Ref 2 is not evidence either way: Cd4HgSe5, CdHgSe2 and CdHg4Se5 are computed cation orderings with no ICSD backing, and they are orderings of the same tetrahedral framework rather than competing structures.

solid_solution_axis.note: Cd/(Cd+Hg) spans 0.21-0.35 -- the narrow-gap HgCdSe alloy field. The chunk file did not flag this axis, but Cd and Hg are both group 12 and share the cation site, so the band gap rather than the structure is what x sets.

dopant_roles.basis: Cr0.0003-0.03Cd0.21Hg0.79Se, and the curator records 'dopant:Cr' -- a 3d transition metal on the tetrahedral cation site.
Curator 'dopant:Co'; same cation site.
Curator 'dopant:Fe'; same cation site.

basis: Four distinct intermetallics share this host and the seed's cacu5 covers only one of them. CeNi (8 samples, the single-crystal thermopower paper) is the CrB-type orthorhombic chain compound, MP Cmcm (63) mp-21188 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD refs. CeNi2 (5 samples) is the cubic MgCu2 Laves phase, mp-1654, 17 ICSD refs. CeNi5 (3 samples, plus the Ga-substituted one) is the CaCu5 type P6/mmm mp-1910, 15 refs -- the seed's hypothesis, right for those alone. Ce7Ni3 (2 samples) is the Th7Fe3 type P6_3mc mp-1106354 and has no taxonomy entry, so it goes to unresolved_crystalline. CeNi15 is not a known line compound and reads as CeNi5 with excess Ni or a transcription error; it needs the paper. Split by the Ni:Ce ratio.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce(Ni0.965Ga0.035)5 -- Ga on the Ni sublattice of the CaCu5-type member, used to tune the 4f instability the paper is about.

basis: The host is MnxFe3-xO4 and the Mn-Zn ferrite series the curator writes as Mn0.58-x/2Zn0.37-x/2MxFe2.05O4 -- cubic spinel ferrites throughout, MP Mn(FeO2)2 Fd-3m (227) mp-18750 with 2 ICSD references, and the papers measure sintered (Mn,Co)Fe2O4 and MnxFe3-xO4. MnFe2O4 is partially inverse, i.e. the Mn/Fe split over tetrahedral and octahedral sites varies with processing, but that is a site-occupancy question for stage 2 and not a different prototype. MP's remaining entries (Mn13Fe11O32 P-1, Mn19Fe17O48 C2/m) are computed cation orderings of the same oxide framework. One curator entry reads 'MnFe2O4, alpha-Fe2O3', so at least one sample carries a corundum second phase.

dopant_roles.basis: The Mn-Zn ferrite series in 12 compositions: Zn2+ has a strong tetrahedral-site preference, so it displaces Mn from the A site.
Mn0.48Zn0.27Nb0.2Fe2.05O4 -- a pentavalent octahedral-site additive in the Mn-Zn ferrite series.
Same M-series of the curator formula, octahedral site.
Mn1-xCdxFe2O4 per the curator: Cd2+ is another tetrahedral-site substituent.

basis: Every composition is FeV1-xNbxSb, mostly at the FeV0.6Nb0.4Sb composition the papers name in their titles -- the 18-electron MgAgAs-type half-Heusler, with V and Nb sharing the group-V site to scatter phonons by mass and strain fluctuation (the second paper's subject). Neither reference covers this host, so the call is from composition plus the paper titles, all three of which say half-Heusler or name FeV0.6Nb0.4Sb.

solid_solution_axis.note: Nb/(Nb+V) spans 0.20-0.75 over 19 compositions, both ends the same prototype; x sets the mass disorder and the lattice parameter, not the structure.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe0.99Co0.01V0.6Nb0.4Sb -- Co on the Fe site adds one electron per substitution and is the carrier-concentration variable of the third paper.
Fe(V0.6Nb0.4)1-yTiySb: Ti is one group lower than V, so it removes an electron -- p-type doping on the same site, not isovalent alloying.
Group-IV substituent on the group-V site: both an acceptor and a heavy mass defect.
As for Zr, with a larger mass contrast.

basis: The host is FeV1-xTixSb, 9 of 22 samples at FeV0.8Ti0.4Sb, and the papers are titled for fine-grained FeVSb half-Heusler alloys -- the MgAgAs-type C1b structure with Ti substituting V. No reference line exists for this host, so the call rests on composition and the paper titles. Note for stage 2 that FeV0.8Ti0.4Sb puts 1.2 atoms on the group-V site: either the nominal formula is off-stoichiometric on purpose (this family tolerates and is often tuned by it) or it is a transcription of Fe(V0.8Ti0.2)Sb, and the paper should settle which.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe(V0.8Hf0.2)1-xTixSb -- a heavy group-IV substituent on the V site, added for mass-fluctuation phonon scattering as much as for doping.
Same-group 4d substituent on the V site: isovalent, so it changes mass and lattice parameter rather than carrier count.

basis: The seed's homologous phase is present but is not the dominant one. InGaZn0.5O4 -- 12 of 22 samples, all films -- is the In:Ga:Zn = 1:1:0.5 sputter-target ratio used for amorphous IGZO, and the second paper is explicitly 'Analysis of thermoelectric properties of amorphous InGaZnO thin film'. InGaZnO4, InGaO3(ZnO) and InGaO3(ZnO)2 (5 samples) are the crystalline InMO3(ZnO)n homologous superlattice of the polytypoid-nanowire paper, which TEDesignLab backs with Zn4InGaO7 P6_3/mmc mp-1194209. InGaZnO7 (5 samples) cannot be charge-balanced as a crystalline phase with In3+/Ga3+/Zn2+, so it reads as a nominal film composition and belongs with the amorphous group. The taxonomy's own note says composition cannot separate a-IGZO from crystalline InGaZnO4, so the split here is made on sample form and paper, and 15 of 22 samples are films.

LiV2O4 is 10 of 22 samples and is the heavy-fermion cubic spinel -- MP LiV2O4 Fd-3m (227) mp-19394 with 15 ICSD references, more than any other Li-V-O entry, and the third paper is on metallic LiV2O4 single crystals. So the spinel half of the seed is confirmed and the vanadium_bronze half is rejected: nothing in this host is an AxV2O5 or AxV4O11 mixed-valence bronze. What the other five compositions are is LiVO3, its Cr2O3-doped ceramics and (K0.2Li0.8)VO3 -- alkali metavanadate chains of V5+, the family the first paper's ferroelectric potassium and caesium vanadates belong to. That had no taxonomy entry, so metavanadate_chain was proposed before use. Split on the Li:V ratio, 1:2 for the spinel and 1:1 for the metavanadate. Note that MP's hull ordering would prefer LiV2O5 or LiVO2 here; neither matches a composition in this host.

dopant_roles.basis: (Cr2O3)x(LiVO3)100-x for x = 0.025-3.0 -- Cr3+ on the V site of the metavanadate ceramics measured in the second paper.
(K0.20Li0.80)VO3 -- alkali-site substitution in the metavanadate, bridging to the KVO3 end member of the same family.
Divalent on the alkali site; the V site cannot be excluded from composition alone.

basis: 9 of 22 samples are plain NiO and the rest are Li-, Ga-, In-, Al- or Na-doped NiO at the percent level, with the curator spelling out '1%Al doped NiO' and '0.1%Ga doped NiO' -- rocksalt NiO, MP Fm-3m (225) mp-19009 at hull 0.000 with 32 ICSD references against nothing comparable. The third paper is titled for a high-performance p-type NiO thermoelectric. Below its 523 K Neel temperature NiO is very slightly rhombohedrally distorted by magnetostriction, which falls inside the 124-776 K window but is a distortion of the same rocksalt prototype, so no phase split is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: Ni1-xLixO at x = 0.03-0.09: Li+ for Ni2+ creates Ni3+ holes and is the classic acceptor that makes NiO a p-type thermoelectric -- the subject of the first paper.
Curator '0.1%Ga doped NiO' and '1%Ga doped NiO'; trivalent cation on the octahedral Ni site.
Curator '1%Al doped NiO'; trivalent on the Ni site.
Trivalent on the Ni site, same series as Ga and Al.
Monovalent acceptor on the Ni site, as for Li but oversized.
'A0.01NiO' is a placeholder for an unnamed dopant in the source table, not an element.

basis: All 22 samples are Ta4SiTe4 with P, Mo, Ti or Sb substituted at the tenth-of-a-percent to percent level, and the papers name M4SiTe4 (M = Ta, Nb) and 'van der Waals crystal Ta4SiTe4' directly. This is the quasi-one-dimensional needle crystal built from Si-centred Ta4 metal-chain columns sheathed in Te, MP Ta4SiTe4 Pbam (55) mp-28509 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references and the only entry for the chemistry. The taxonomy had no home for it -- nbse3_chain is a different MX3 chain family -- so ta4site4_chain was proposed before use. The 10-346 K window is where the family's large low-temperature power factor sits and crosses no transition.

dopant_roles.basis: Ta4Si1-xPxTe4 at x = 0.005-0.02 -- P on the chain-centre Si site is the hole-doping variable of the phosphorus-doped paper.
The curator writes (Ta1-xMox)4Si(Te1-ySby)4 -- Mo on the Ta chain site removes an electron, the hole doping of the M4SiTe4 paper.
(Ta0.999Ti0.001)4SiTe4 -- group-IV substituent on the Ta chain site.
The y variable of (Ta1-xMox)4Si(Te1-ySby)4: Sb on the Te sheath site, also a hole dopant.

basis: Every composition is LaFe1-yCoyAsO0.89F0.11 with y = 0.2-0.5 -- the ZrCuSiAs-type '1111' iron arsenide, alternating La2O2 and FeAs layers, and the papers are titled for LaFe1-yCoyAsO1-xFx across the superconducting-to-magnetic crossover. No reference line exists for this host, so the call is from composition plus the papers. Undoped LaFeAsO has a tetragonal-to-orthorhombic distortion near 150 K, inside the 10-301 K window, but at 11% F plus 20% or more Co on the Fe site that transition is suppressed; it is worth confirming from the papers rather than recording a phase split here.

dopant_roles.basis: O0.89F0.11 in every composition: F on the oxygen site of the La2O2 layer is the electron-doping variable of the 1111 family, not an impurity -- the taxonomy records this for zrcusias_1111.

basis: The host is Ba8AuxGe46-x with x = 3-6, 9 of 21 samples at Ba8Au5.3Ge40.7, and the third paper is titled 'Atomic Interactions in the p-Type Clathrate I Ba8Au5.3Ge40.7'. MP's Ba4Ge20Au3 Pm-3n (223) mp-21839 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references is that same Ba8Au6Ge40 type-I clathrate cell. Au is not a dopant here: it substitutes into the Ge framework and sets the electron count, which is why the Au content is the variable being scanned. The other MP entries (BaGe2Au5 Pnma, BaGeAu3 I4mm) are Au-rich line compounds no composition approaches.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba8Au5Ga1Ge40 -- Ga enters the clathrate framework alongside Au and adjusts the electron count per the Zintl rule, as the Ba8AuxGa16-xGe30 paper title implies.

basis: Most of this host is SrCo1-xFexO3 at or near the O3 stoichiometry (SrFe0.5Co0.5O3, SrCo0.6Fe0.4O3 and the Mo/Sb-substituted variants), where Co keeps the vacancies disordered and the structure is the cubic ABO3 perovskite -- so the seed's brownmillerite is not right for the host as a whole. It is right for one corner: SrCo0.25Fe0.75O2.69 (3 samples) is the most Fe-rich and most reduced composition, and brownmillerite-type vacancy ordering towards SrFeO2.5 is genuine there, so the split is by oxygen content and Co:Fe ratio. Sr4Fe4.5Co1.5O13 is a third structure -- the Sr4Fe6O13-type layered intergrowth of the first paper -- with no taxonomy entry, so it is parked in unresolved_crystalline. Ref 2 cannot arbitrate: all five entries are computed Sr-Fe-Co-O supercells with no ICSD backing.

dopant_roles.basis: SrFe0.475Co0.475Mo0.05O3 -- a high-valence B-site substituent used to stabilise the cubic perovskite against vacancy ordering.
SrFe0.475Co0.475Sb0.05O3, same B site and role.
Pentavalent B-site substituent.
SrCo0.95Ti0.05O3 in the cobalt-reduction paper: Ti4+ on the octahedral B site.
Tetravalent B-site substituent, larger than Ti.
Tetravalent B-site substituent.
Trivalent B-site substituent.
B-site transition metal.
Isovalent A-site substitution, which mostly changes the tolerance factor.
Lone-pair cation on the A site; in related cobaltites Bi can instead form its own rocksalt-type block, so this needs the paper.

basis: La2-xSrxCuO4 at x = 0.35-0.50 (9 of 21 samples, and the 'single-layer copper oxides' thermopower paper) is the n=1 Ruddlesden-Popper T-phase cuprate, so the seed is confirmed for the larger part of the host. The rest is a different structure: La2Sr6Cu8O16 and La2Sr6Cu8O17.6 (6 samples) reduce to (La0.25Sr0.75)CuO2 and (La0.25Sr0.75)CuO2.2, the ACuO2 infinite-layer stoichiometry, and they come from the paper on 'new conductive copper oxides' with their crystal structures. I record that as infinite_layer_cuprate with medium confidence: the oxygen-excess O17.6 member may be a distinct intergrowth rather than a doped infinite-layer phase, and only the paper settles it. Ref 2 offers only computed Sr-La-Cu-O supercells with no ICSD backing, so it neither confirms nor refutes either reading.

dopant_roles.basis: La1.61Sr0.39Cu0.94Ti0.06O4 -- Ti4+ on the in-plane Cu site, which removes carriers from the CuO2 sheet.
B-site substituent in the CuO2 plane.
B-site substituent in the CuO2 plane.
B-site substituent in the CuO2 plane.

basis: 9 of 21 samples are NiFe2O4 outright and the rest are Cd-, Cu-, Zn- or Al-substituted nickel ferrite -- the inverse cubic spinel, MP Fe2NiO4 Fd-3m (227) mp-24941 with 4 ICSD references, the best-attested entry for the chemistry. Its hull of 0.281 is a 2019-dump artefact for magnetic oxides of this kind and is not evidence against it, exactly as for Sb2Te3; the competing Fe(NiO2)2 Fd-3m entry is the same spinel framework at a different cation ratio. Two compositions are polymer composites (the curator's 'PC/2%NiFe2O4'), where the ferrite is a filler in polycarbonate; the inorganic phase is still spinel, so the host label holds.

dopant_roles.basis: Cd1-xNixFe2O4 per the curator: Cd2+ has a strong tetrahedral-site preference and displaces Ni from the A site.
Ni0.8Cu0.2Fe2O4 -- Cu2+ on the octahedral Ni site of the inverse spinel; the first paper is on mixed Ni-Cu nanoferrites.
NiAlxFe2-xO4 per the curator: Al3+ replaces Fe3+, chiefly on octahedral sites.
Tetrahedral-site substituent, as in Ni-Zn ferrites.
Present in 3 compositions with no visible formula showing where it sits; boron is not a plausible spinel cation, so a sintering aid or grain-boundary phase is more likely. Needs the paper.

basis: MoTe2 and Mo1-xNbxTe2 (9 samples) are the 2H alpha-MoTe2 layered dichalcogenide -- TEDesignLab Te2Mo P6_3/mmc (194) mp-602, hull 0.000, 4 ICSD refs -- so the seed holds for the dichalcogenide compositions. Mo3Te4 (2 samples, with its own paper) is not one of them: it is the Chevrel-type cluster telluride, MP Te4Mo3 R-3 (148) mp-8601 at hull 0.000, which the taxonomy already carries as chevrel, so the host splits on the Te:Mo ratio. The 1T'/beta polymorph is real and named in the 'rich structural phase diagram' paper, but 2H converts to it only above roughly 1150 K, beyond this 10-825 K window, and it is retained at room temperature only by quenching or Nb doping -- so it goes in other_polymorphs rather than into the thermal sequence.

other_polymorphs.note: beta/1T' MoTe2, P2_1/m, 1 ICSD ref at hull 0.016. The high-temperature form above ~1150 K, kept at room temperature only by quenching or Nb doping, and itself distorting to the Td phase (Pmn2_1) near 250 K. The taxonomy has no 1T' distorted-octahedral entry, so it is recorded as unresolved_crystalline rather than forced into mos2_2h.
P-6m2 Te2Mo at hull 0.002 with no ICSD references -- the single-layer 1H stacking variant, a computational entry rather than a bulk phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Mo1-xNbxTe2 at x = 0.05-0.08: Nb removes one electron per substitution, the p-type knob, and is also known to stabilise the 1T' polymorph -- so the doping level and the polymorph question are linked here.
Iodine in transition-metal ditelluride crystal growth is a vapour-transport agent; residue rather than a lattice substituent.

basis: Every composition is NaxV2O5 with x = 0.83-1.00, optionally with Ca on the Na site -- alpha'-NaV2O5, which is the exemplar of the taxonomy's own vanadium_bronze entry, and the single paper is on electronic transport in this layered bronze with correlation and disorder effects. MP NaV2O5 Pmmn (59) mp-19111 carries 12 ICSD references, more than any other Na-V-O entry; NaVO3 (5 refs) and NaVO2 (3 refs) are different stoichiometries that no composition here matches. The Na deficiency in Na0.84V2O5 is the carrier-concentration variable of this family, not an impurity. The 34 K charge-ordering transition of alpha'-NaV2O5 sits below the 88 K start of the measured window, so nothing is crossed.

dopant_roles.basis: Na1-xCaxV2O5 at x = 0.10-0.17: a divalent cation on the alkali site, which changes both the V valence and the site disorder the paper is about.

basis: The host is near-equiatomic TiNi shape-memory alloy (Ti50Ni50 through Ti48.4Ni51.6) and the papers are titled for TiNi shape-memory and Ti-Ni internal friction, so the 11-396 K window spans the martensitic transformation: monoclinic B19' martensite at the low end, cubic B2 austenite at the high end. The seed offered only b2_cscl, the parent, which left the low-temperature end of every curve without a prototype -- so b19prime_martensite was proposed before use and the record carries both phases. The references favour the martensite: MP TiNi P2_1/m mp-1048 has 21 ICSD references at hull 0.001, the most of any Ti-Ni entry, and B2 TiNi has no entry of its own in the list at all, which is why its mp_id is left null rather than guessed. Confidence is medium because the transition temperature is not a host-level constant: Ms is near 330 K for Ti50Ni50 but is suppressed below 200 K by a percent of excess Ni, so the Ni-rich compositions here are austenitic over most of the window. Ti2Ni and TiNi3 exist in this chemistry with 7 ICSD references each, but no composition is far enough from equiatomic to be either.

dopant_roles.basis: The Cu-substitution paper puts Cu on the Ni sublattice of the B2 parent; it lowers the transformation hysteresis and can route the transformation through a B19 orthorhombic intermediate, so it bears directly on which phase is present.

basis: The host is PbSe1-xSx with x = 0.10-0.60, mostly Cl- or Cu-doped and often written with excess Pb (Pb1.1234Se1S0.12Cl0.0068) -- PbS and PbSe are both rocksalt and fully miscible, so the prototype is the same at every point on the anion axis and the papers are PbS/PbSe nanostructure and PbTe1-ySy thermoelectric studies. Ref 2 has no ICSD-backed entry for the ternary: Pb2SeS R-3m, Pb4Se3S P4/mmm and Pb4SeS3 R-3m are computed anion orderings of the rocksalt lattice, which is consistent with rocksalt rather than an alternative to it. The Pb excess on several compositions is non-stoichiometry -- metal-rich PbSe is n-type by native defects -- and should be treated as such in stage 3, not as a dopant fraction.

solid_solution_axis.note: S/(S+Se) spans 0.10-0.60 with a median of 0.15, so most compositions are PbSe with S alloyed in; both end members are rocksalt, so the axis sets the gap and the lattice thermal conductivity, not the structure.

dopant_roles.basis: Introduced as PbCl2 at the 0.6-0.8% level: Cl on the anion site is the standard n-type donor for lead chalcogenides.
Cu in lead chalcogenides is normally an interstitial donor rather than a cation substituent, though substitution on the Pb site cannot be excluded from composition alone.
Pb1Se0.88S0.12Bi0.003 -- trivalent donor on the Pb site.

basis: Tl4SnTe3 (4 samples), Tl9SnTe6 and the Tl7.95-8.05Sn1.95-2.05Te6 pair (5 samples) are all the same Tl5-xSnxTe3 line written per 3 or 6 Te -- the Tl5Te3 type, MP Tl4SnTe3 I4/mcm (140) mp-3019 with 5 ICSD references, plus the I4/m superstructure variant mp-1216727 -- so the seed is confirmed for 9 of the 21 samples and the high-ZT paper is about that phase. The seed does not cover the rest: Tl2SnTe3 (3 samples, MP Pnma mp-28662) and Tl2SnTe5 (2 samples, MP I4/mcm mp-28843) are distinct ternary Tl-Sn-Te structure types, each with its own ICSD reference, and neither has a taxonomy entry, so they go to unresolved_crystalline. Split by stoichiometry, which the taxonomy's own discriminate_from note for this prototype already asks for.

dopant_roles.basis: The Tl5Te3 framework hosts Sn, Bi or Pb on the same trivalent-to-tetravalent site -- Tl9BiTe6 is the isostructural end member -- so Bi here substitutes for Sn rather than acting as a dilute impurity.

basis: CeNi2Al3 and its Cu-substituted variants are 9 of the 20 samples and are the PrNi2Al3 type -- an ordered CaCu5 superstructure, hexagonal P6/mmm, which MP has as CeAl3Ni2 P6/mmm mp-20338 at hull 0.000. The rest of the host is three further intermetallics with no taxonomy entry: CeNi2Al5 (3 samples, MP CeAl5Ni2 Immm mp-4817, 4 ICSD refs), CeNiAl4 (3 samples, the Kondo-lattice thermal-conductivity paper, MP CeAl4Ni Cmcm mp-30750, the YNiAl4 type) and CeNiAl (2 samples, MP CeAlNi P-62m mp-11351, the ZrNiAl/Fe2P type with 3 ICSD refs). All three go to unresolved_crystalline and the ZrNiAl and YNiAl4 types are worth adding in v4 -- they recur across the Ce-Ni-Al and related heavy-fermion hosts. Split by the Al:Ni ratio.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce(Ni1-xCux)2Al3 -- Cu on the Ni site is the variable in two of the papers, tuning the heavy-fermion state; the compositions show x up to 0.1.
Transition-metal site of the same structure.

basis: Ten of the twelve compositions carry the curator's _IQC suffix at Al64-65Cu19-21Ru15-17, which is the stable icosahedral Al-Cu-Ru quasicrystal field, and two of the papers are on low-temperature transport in Al-Cu-Ru quasicrystalline alloys and on modelling icosahedral conductivity. Al65Cu20Ru15 without the suffix is the same nominal composition and is almost certainly icosahedral too. There is no periodic structure to assign: the taxonomy flags this prototype for special handling, and MP's only entry, Al7Cu2Ru P4/mnc mp-1214866 (hull 0.000, no ICSD reference), is a periodic phase that can serve as an approximant in stage 2 provided the record says so rather than claiming it is the structure.

La1-xCaxCoO3 with x = 0.3-0.6 is 18 of the 20 samples -- the ABO3 cobaltite perovskite with La and Ca sharing the A site, and the 'structural distortions' paper is about exactly that series. The other two compositions are deliberate two-phase composites, (Ca3Co4O9)32.03(La0.8Sr0.2CoO3)67.97 and (LaCo0.8Ni0.1Fe0.1O3)3.3(Ca3Co4O9)0.40, which pair the perovskite with the misfit cobaltite, so misfit_cobaltite and composite_multiphase are both genuinely present and those two need splitting out. MP offers CaLa(CoO3)2 Fm-3m mp-1227082 with no ICSD backing, which is an ordered A-site arrangement of the same perovskite rather than a competing structure, and CaLa3(CoO4)2 at a Ruddlesden-Popper stoichiometry no composition here reaches.

dopant_roles.basis: La0.8Sr0.2CoO3 inside the composite composition: divalent on the A site, the same hole-doping role Ca plays in the main series.
LaCo0.8Ni0.1Fe0.1O3 -- B-site transition metal.
Same composition, B site.

basis: CeNi2Ge2 and its Pd-substituted variants are 9 of the 20 samples and are the ThCr2Si2 type -- MP Ce(NiGe)2 I4/mmm (139) mp-3325 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references -- so the seed is right for the largest group, and the CeNi2Ge2 anisotropy paper is about that phase. It does not cover the rest. CeNiGe2 (5 samples) is the CeNiSi2 type, MP Cmcm (63) mp-3541 with 5 ICSD references -- a layered orthorhombic structure, not a 122 -- and Ce2Ni3Ge5 (U2Co3Si5 type) and Ce3NiGe2 each have one sample from the Kondo-lattice transport paper. None of those three has a taxonomy entry, so they are recorded as unresolved_crystalline; CeNiSi2-type is the one worth adding in v4, since it is a common Ce-based ternary germanide and silicide. Split by the Ni:Ge ratio.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce(Ni1-xPdx)2Ge2 at x = 0.06-0.12 -- same-group substitution on the transition-metal site, used to tune the quantum-critical state in the first paper.
CeNi2Si2 and CeNi2Ge2 are isostructural end members, so Si on the Ge site is isovalent site alloying rather than doping.

basis: The whole host is CoSbS with Ni, Se or Mo substituted at a few per cent -- paracostibite, MP CoSbS Pbca (61) mp-5881 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, and the second paper is titled for the electronic and thermoelectric properties of CoSbS. The two other CoSbS entries, P2_13 mp-1102443 (the ullmannite-type ordering) and Pmn2_1 mp-4962, carry one ICSD reference each at hull 0.010 and are alternative anion orderings of the same MXY framework rather than phases reached by heating, so they go in other_polymorphs.

other_polymorphs.note: P2_13 CoSbS, 1 ICSD ref at hull 0.010 -- the ullmannite-type Sb/S ordering of the same framework, not a thermal phase of paracostibite.
Pmn2_1 CoSbS, 1 ICSD ref at hull 0.010 -- another ordering variant, listed so the polymorph count is not mistaken for a thermal sequence.

dopant_roles.basis: Co1-xNixSbS at x = 0.02-0.08, present in 11 compositions: Ni on the Co site adds electrons and is the n-type carrier knob the first paper measures.
Same-group anion substitution, which tunes the gap and the lattice thermal conductivity without adding carriers.
The intermediate-band paper modifies the transition-metal site; Mo there is a substituent rather than a second phase.

basis: Two prototypes share this host and the seed names the smaller one. Eleven of the twelve compositions are Cu3Sb(Se,S)4 with Sn or Ge on the Sb site -- the famatinite/permingeatite I-42m structure, and the first paper is titled 'High thermoelectric figure of merit in the Cu3SbSe4-Cu3SbS4 solid solution', which is that family end to end. The remaining composition, Cu12Sb3.6Bi0.4S10Se3 (8 samples), is tetrahedrite: 12 Cu, 4 Sb-site atoms and 13 anions is the Cu12Sb4S13 formula with Se on part of the anion sublattice. So tetrahedrite is confirmed but only for one composition, and the host splits on the Cu:Sb ratio (3:1 famatinite versus 12:4 tetrahedrite). Neither reference covers this host, so the call rests on the compositions and the paper titles.

solid_solution_axis.note: S/(S+Se) spans 0.12-0.85 over 12 compositions. It is the Cu3SbSe4-Cu3SbS4 solid solution for the famatinite compositions -- isostructural end members, so the prototype does not change along it -- while for the tetrahedrite composition the Se simply occupies part of the 13-anion sublattice.

dopant_roles.basis: Cu3Sb0.94Sn0.06Se3.5S0.5 -- Sn for Sb removes an electron and is the standard p-type acceptor in Cu3SbSe4.
Cu3Sb0.97Ge0.03Se2.8S1.2 -- same acceptor role on the Sb site.
Cu12Sb3.6Bi0.4S10Se3: Bi on the Sb site of the tetrahedrite composition, where it is a lone-pair substituent rather than a carrier dopant.

basis: ZnFe2O4 (5 samples) and the Li0.5-0.5xZnxLayFe2.5-0.5x-yO4 lithium-zinc ferrites named in the curator detail are all cubic spinel: MP Zn(FeO2)2 Fd-3m mp-19313 carries 31 ICSD references at hull 0.000, and Zn0.945Fe1.78O3.71 is the same AB2O4 line written off-stoichiometric. Zn0.750Fe0.171O is not spinel at all -- one oxygen per cation with Fe at a fifth of the Zn content is the Fe-enriched wurtzite ZnO of the first paper. So the host holds two prototypes and splits on the O:cation ratio, 1 for wurtzite against 4:3 for spinel.
reference_disagreement: The reference line covers only the Zn-Fe-O ternary phases and offers nothing for Fe-doped ZnO, so the wurtzite half of this host carries no mp_id here. That is a gap in the evidence rather than a disagreement: the spinel entries themselves match.

dopant_roles.basis: Li0.5-0.5xZnxLayFe2.5-0.5x-yO4: monovalent Li on the octahedral B site of the ferrite balances Fe3+. It is a formula component of the lithium ferrite, not a dilute impurity.
y = 0.04 in the same series. La3+ is large for the octahedral Fe site and sits near its solubility limit, so part of it may segregate as a LaFeO3 second phase.
Divalent cation on the tetrahedral A site of the spinel.
The curator detail says the ZnFe2O4 nanoparticles sit in multiwall carbon nanotubes containing Ni residuals, so Ni is growth-catalyst residue from the nanotubes and is not in the oxide lattice.

basis: The host is elemental niobium, one composition and 20 samples, measured as a reference metal -- the curator detail says the absolute Seebeck coefficient of niobium obtained from the Nb-Pt curve, and the papers are on the intrinsic thermopower of the group VB metals. Body-centred cubic W (A2) type, MP Nb Im-3m mp-75 with 18 ICSD references at hull 0.000, and bcc is the only phase up to melting, so the 10-1407 K window crosses nothing. The taxonomy already names Nb under this entry for exactly this case.

other_polymorphs.note: fcc Nb: one ICSD reference at hull 0.342, reachable in strained films but never by heating bulk bcc Nb.

basis: Pr0.67TiO3 and Sr0.15Pr0.567TiO3 are 18 of the 20 samples and are A-site-deficient rare-earth titanate perovskites -- the Pr analogue of La2/3TiO3, where the A-site vacancies order into a doubled orthorhombic cell -- while PrTiO3 itself is the GdFeO3-distorted ABO3 end member. Every composition is ABO3 in oxygen with Ti alone on the B site, so the prototype is perovskite throughout; what varies is A-site occupancy, which is the Ti3+/Ti4+ carrier-count knob rather than a change of structure.
reference_disagreement: MP ranks Pr2Ti2O7 P2_1 (mp-15201) and Pr2TiO5 Pnma first for this chemistry. Neither is what these samples are: both are fully oxidised Ti4+ phases of a different stoichiometry, while the samples are reduced A-site-deficient ABO3. MP does carry PrTiO3 but at R-3c (mp-753948, hull 0.029), whereas the ambient structure of the rare-earth titanate perovskites is the Pnma tilt system, so no mp_id is recorded rather than adopting a space group I do not think these samples have.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr0.15Pr0.567TiO3, 9 samples. Divalent Sr on the 12-coordinate A site is an aliovalent substituent that sets the Ti3+ fraction; at 15% of the A site it is an alloying level rather than dilute doping.
Pr0.6Ca0.1TiO3, same A-site role.

basis: (SnS)1.2(TiS2)2 and its Cu-, Cl-, Sb- and Ag-substituted variants are the SnS-TiS2 misfit layer compound end to end -- the composition strings are already written as the two subsystems, the second paper is titled (MS)1+x(TiS2)2 for M = Pb, Bi, Sn, and the first calls it a natural superlattice. Sn1.2Ti0.8S3 is the same phase collapsed into a single formula.
reference_disagreement: MP offers only Ti3Sn5S12 Pm mp-1217186, a computed ternary at hull 0.014 that is not the misfit composite. As the taxonomy notes for this prototype, an incommensurate two-subsystem structure has no single MP entry, so mp_id stays null rather than taking the nearest formula.

dopant_roles.basis: (SnS)1.2(Cu0.02Ti0.98S2)2 puts Cu on the Ti site of the TiS2 subsystem explicitly.
Chloride doping is the subject of the third paper; halide on the anion site is the electron donor, introduced as SnCl2 or CuCl.
(Sb0.04Sn0.96S)1.2 places Sb inside the rocksalt-like SnS subsystem.
Monovalent cation in the SnS subsystem; part of the multisite alloying study.
Early transition metal on the TiS2 layer site.

basis: All 19 samples are Ce(Ni1-xCux)2Al3 at x = 0.2-0.6, the Kondo-lattice aluminide of the three papers. RT2Al3 of this family is the PrNi2Al3 type -- an ordered ternary derivative of CaCu5 in which the transition metal and Al take the two distinct Cu sites of the hexagonal AB5 cell. The taxonomy has the CaCu5 parent but not the ordered derivative, so prni2al3_ordered_cacu5 is proposed before use. Confidence is medium because the Cu-rich end of RCu2Al3 is reported in the tetragonal BaAl4/ThCr2Si2 variant instead, and x here reaches 0.6.
reference_disagreement: MP has only CeAl(CuNi)2 Cmmm mp-1226666 (hull 0.023) and Amm2 mp-1226667 (hull 0.098), both computed orderings with no ICSD backing and neither at the RT2Al3 stoichiometry of these samples. The space group recorded here comes from the structure literature, not from the reference line, and mp_id is left null.

basis: Al65-74 with Ni and Co each near 10-20 at.% is the decagonal Al-Ni-Co field, and the papers say so directly: intrinsic anisotropic transport of a decagonal quasicrystal, heat transport in aluminium-based quasicrystals, and a single-grain decagonal Al-Ni-Co. The seed is confirmed with one qualification worth recording -- this host is decagonal, periodic along one axis and quasiperiodic in the plane, while the entry is written around icosahedral Al-Pd-Re. That anisotropy between the two directions is the point of the first paper.
reference_disagreement: The MP entries offered (Al18Co5Ni3 Cm, Al2CoNi P4/mmm, Al9Co2Ni Immm) are ordinary periodic aluminides, not the decagonal phase. Following the taxonomy note for this prototype, no periodic structure is adopted and mp_id stays null; stage 2 should map to an approximant and say so.

basis: GaAs is 13 of the 19 samples and (AlAs)1(GaAs)10 is an AlAs/GaAs multilayer of the same lattice, so the host is zincblende throughout: TEDesignLab gives GaAs F-43m mp-2534 with 29 ICSD references at hull 0.000, the highest-attested entry in the chemistry.

other_polymorphs.note: The nanowire and epitaxial polytype of GaAs, 2 ICSD references against 29 for F-43m. Films are present in this host so it is worth listing, but heating bulk GaAs does not produce it.

dopant_roles.basis: (AlAs)1(GaAs)10 is a multilayer film, so Al is a separate epitaxial layer of the isostructural end member rather than a dilute substituent in GaAs. The curator detail confirms the multilayer.

note: The curator details record indium and bismuth ion implantation for several films (In to a target 1e18 per cm3, Bi doses of 1.4-5.6e16), and the papers are about embedded In nanocrystals. Those elements do not appear in the parsed composition strings, so no dopant role is recorded for them here even though the papers turn on them.

basis: In0.53Ga0.47As, lattice-matched to InP, with Al added as the InGaAlAs quaternary -- all zincblende III-V films and superlattices. The rare earths are not in the lattice: ErAs and TbAs are semimetallic rocksalt nanoparticles deliberately embedded in the matrix, which is what all three papers are about, and the curator detail gives the ErAs concentration as 0.3% in all samples.
reference_disagreement: The MP entries (In2GaAs3 I-4m2, InGaAs2 P-4m2 and R3m, InGa5As4 R3m, hulls 0.027-0.135) are all computed In/Ga orderings. The samples are a random zincblende alloy at a fixed 53:47 ratio, not an ordered cell, so mp_id is left null.

dopant_roles.basis: (TbAs)0.0636InGaAs and (TbAs)1.12(In0.53Ga0.47As)98.88: TbAs forms rocksalt nanoinclusions in the matrix. Deliberate rather than a contaminant, but it is a second phase, not a substituent.
ErAs nanoparticles at 0.3%, the semimetal/semiconductor nanocomposite the second and third papers are built on.
In0.53Ga0.4Al0.06As: Al on the group-III site of the quaternary barrier layer, isostructural and isoelectronic.

basis: LaBaCo2O5.5 (6 samples) is the A-site-ordered 112 double perovskite -- alternating La and Ba layers with ordered oxygen vacancies in the La plane -- and the first paper is titled for the layered perovskite. But La0.5Ba0.5CoO3 (6 samples) is the same cation ratio as the disordered cubic perovskite at full oxygen content, and La0.7Ba0.3CoO3 is off the 1:1 ratio ordering needs. So the host holds both prototypes, and the cation ratio cannot separate them: only the oxygen content (O5.5 against O6) and the synthesis can, which makes this a case where the split rule has to use oxygen and the ordered/disordered call may need the paper.
reference_disagreement: MP BaLa(CoO3)2 P4/mmm mp-24855 rests on a single ICSD reference at hull 0.072, and the remaining entries for the chemistry are large computed Ba-La-Co-O cells at hulls of 0.04-0.11. The evidence is thin on both sides here rather than contradictory.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba0.4La0.6Co0.8Fe0.2O3: B-site substitution at 20% of the Co site, an alloying level typical of the mixed ionic-electronic conductor compositions.
La0.3Ba0.7Co0.8Nb0.2O3; the third paper is about the effect of Nb5+ content, so it is a donor on the B site.
Tetravalent B-site substituent.
B-site substituent; single composition.
Rare-earth A site; the second paper covers R = La, Pr and Nd in the same series.

basis: PrO1-xFxBiS2 at x = 0.5 and 0.7 is the BiS2-based layered superconductor: BiS2 conducting bilayers alternating with PrO/F blocking layers in the P4/nmm stacking this entry describes, and F-for-O is the electron-doping variable the single paper scans. Both compositions are that one phase, so nothing here needs splitting.
reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this chemistry at all -- neither TEDesignLab nor MP -- so the space group is from the structure literature and mp_id is null. The measured range is 12-295 K from two curves, which is a magnetotransport study rather than a thermoelectric one.
note: Fluorine is 14 at.% of PrO0.3F0.7BiS2 and so sits above the 5% host/dopant split, which is why it carries no dopant_roles entry. It is nonetheless the doping variable of the family, and stage 3 should treat F-for-O exactly as the zrcusias_1111 notes prescribe.

basis: K2Bi8Se13 with Rb on the K site, Sb or Mn on the Bi site, Te on the Se site and BiCl3 added is the whole host, and the third paper names beta-K2Bi8Se13 directly. It is one of the complex bismuth chalcogenides this entry exists for: a low-symmetry C2/m framework of Bi/Se blocks with K in the tunnels, MP mp-28800 at hull 0.000. Every composition is that one framework, so the host does not split.

other_polymorphs.note: The alpha modification of K2Bi8Se13, P2_1/m at hull 0.030. Alpha and beta are separate synthesis products of the same formula rather than steps in a thermal sequence, and the papers here name beta; which one a given sample is needs the paper.

dopant_roles.basis: K1.5Rb0.5Bi8Se13 and K1.8Rb0.2Bi8Se13. The first paper is titled for site-selective Rb/K distribution, so the alkali sites are not equivalent and stage 2 should record which one.
The curator detail reads K2Bi8Se13 plus 1-4% BiCl3: halide on the anion sublattice, the electron donor of those four samples.
K2Bi7.2Sb0.8Se13: same-valence pnictogen on the Bi framework sites, for mass contrast rather than carriers.
K2(Bi0.95Mn0.05)8Se13, a magnetic substituent on the framework.
K2Bi8(Se0.95Te0.05)13: anion-site alloying.

basis: (BiS)1.2(TiS2)2 with a transition metal on the Ti site or an alkaline earth on the Bi site is all 15 compositions, and the papers name misfit layer compounds and bismuth intercalated BiS/TiS2 explicitly. The composition strings already separate the two incommensurate subsystems, which is what makes the assignment unambiguous.
reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this chemistry, which is expected for an incommensurate composite: it has no single MP entry by construction. mp_id is null.

dopant_roles.basis: (BiS)1.2(Ti0.95Cr0.05S2)2 -- the string places it inside the TiS2 layer. The first paper is the transition-metal substitution study and Cr is its largest series.
Same series, Ti0.95Fe0.05S2 layer.

The second paper is on alkaline earth doping, which goes into the rocksalt-like BiS subsystem, not the TiS2 one.
