basis: C6H7N is the aniline repeat unit and the curator names polyaniline with its CAS number on 13 of the 19 samples, as film, pellet, nanotube and non-nanostructured forms. One composition is different in kind: the curator gives HITP, hexaiminotriphenylene C18H12N6, which with the Ni in the candidate list is Ni3(HITP)2 -- a crystalline 2D pi-d conjugated coordination framework, not a chain polymer. That one is split out under the proposed conductive_mof_2d entry rather than being absorbed into organic_polymer.
reference_disagreement: The MP entries offered (H5CN3 Pbca, HC2N3, H2CN2, and two cyanamide coordination compounds) are small-molecule nitrides and cyanamides matched on the C-H-N element set alone. None of them is a polymer and none is relevant; this is a case where the reference indexing by host system finds chemistry rather than material.

dopant_roles.basis: C6H7NCl0.1: the chloride counter-ion of HCl-protonated emeraldine salt. It sits between chains as the charge-compensating anion -- the doping variable of conducting polyaniline -- rather than on any lattice site.
Ag0.001-0.004(C6H7N): the first paper is titled for Ag nanoparticle/polyaniline composites, so Ag is metallic filler, not a substituent.

Ni is the metal node of the Ni3(HITP)2 composition -- a structural component of that framework rather than a dopant in polyaniline. The role vocabulary has no value for a host constituent that falls under the 5% cut, so it is recorded as unknown with this explanation.
Inorganic filler in a polymer composite; single composition.
Inorganic filler in a polymer composite; single composition.

basis: Both seed hypotheses are right and the host splits cleanly between them on the Eu:Cd ratio. EuCd2Sb2 (8 samples) is the CaAl2Si2-type trigonal Zintl phase, MP Eu(CdSb)2 P-3m1 mp-19774 at hull 0.000. Eu11Cd6Sb12 (4 samples), with its As-, Zn- and Cd-deficient variants, is the 11-6-12 Zintl structure -- a different framework at 1:2 against 11:6 -- and the first two papers are titled for solid-solution Zintl phases of exactly these two families.

dopant_roles.basis: Eu11Cd5ZnSb12 and the Eu(Zn1-xCdx)2Sb2 series of the third paper: Zn and Cd are the same group on the tetrahedral framework site, a continuous solid solution rather than doping.
EuCd1.9Mn0.1Sb2: magnetic substituent on the framework cation site.
Eu11Cd6Sb11As: same-group pnictogen on the anion sublattice.
Divalent rare earth on the Eu site; both form the same AM2Sb2 structure.

basis: (Ce1-xLax)Ni across the full range is the CrB-type equiatomic chain compound the seed names, and it is what the two single-crystal thermopower papers measure. But two other stoichiometries share the host: (Ce0.82La0.18)Ni2 is the C15 Laves phase, and (Ce0.9La0.1)7Ni3 is the Th7Fe3-type hexagonal phase of the third paper, on the heavy-fermion compound Ce7Ni3. The taxonomy had no R7T3 entry, so th7fe3 is proposed before use. Three prototypes here, separated by the Ni:R ratio at 3:7, 1:1 and 2:1.

solid_solution_axis.note: Ce/(Ce+La) spans 0.10-0.90 over 15 compositions. The structure does not change along it -- CeNi and LaNi are both CrB-type -- but the physics does: dilute Ce in LaNi is a single-ion Kondo impurity, which is what the paper on dilute Kondo type Ce compounds measures, while the middle of the range is a concentrated Kondo lattice.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Ce and La are both trivalent rare earths on the same site, so the axis is genuine.

reference_disagreement: MP offers only LaCeNi10 Pmmm mp-1223428, a computed 1:1:10 ordering that matches no composition in this host. mp_id is left null for every phase here.

basis: (Ti,Hf)CoSb1-xSnx is the p-type half-Heusler of all six papers -- nanostructured p-type half-Heuslers, phase-separated half-Heuslers, and the (Ti/Zr/Hf)CoSb series. Every composition is 1:1:1 in (Ti+Hf):Co:(Sb+Sn) on the cubic C1b lattice, with Sn on the Sb site as the acceptor, so one prototype covers the host.

solid_solution_axis.note: Hf/(Hf+Ti) spans 0.25-0.80 over 8 compositions. Both end members are half-Heusler, so the prototype is constant along the axis; the mixing is for point-defect phonon scattering and, in the phase-separation paper, for deliberate spinodal microstructure.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Ti, Zr and Hf are the same group on the same site.

reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this five-element host, so mp_id is null. Stage 2 should resolve the end members TiCoSb and HfCoSb separately rather than seeking one entry for the alloy.

dopant_roles.basis: (Hf0.72Zr0.1Ti0.18)CoSb0.8Sn0.2: a third group-4 element on the same site, part of the (Ti/Zr/Hf) mixing rather than a dopant.
Late transition metal on the Co site, which changes the valence electron count away from 18.
Ni for Co is the electron-donating substitution in MCoSb, and excess Ni also drives partial filling toward the full Heusler.
Chalcogen on the Sb site is the n-type donor, working against the Sn acceptor.
Same donor role on the Sb site.

basis: Co3Sn2-xInxS2 stepped from x = 0.4 to 0.9 is the host end to end: the Co3Sn2S2 shandite, a rhombohedral R-3m structure of Co kagome layers, with In on the Sn site tuning the Fermi level. MP InCo3SnS2 R-3m mp-1077901 sits at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, and the papers name shandite, metal-atom ordering and double substitution in shandites directly.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe on the kagome Co site is the second substitution of the double-substitution paper, and it moves the half-metallic band structure rather than merely adding carriers.
Same-group chalcogen on the anion site.

basis: LaNi1-xCoxO3 over x = 0.3-0.7 is a continuous B-site solid solution between two rhombohedral R-3c perovskites, LaNiO3 and LaCoO3, and the first paper is titled for LaNi1-xCoxO3 solid solutions. One prototype covers every composition, so no split is needed despite the four-element host.
reference_disagreement: MP offers only La2CoNiO6 R-3 mp-1223259, a computed B-site-ordered double perovskite with no ICSD backing. These samples are the disordered solid solution -- x is varied continuously, which a 1:1 ordered compound cannot represent -- so double_perovskite is not used and mp_id is left null.

dopant_roles.basis: A third transition metal on the same B site; single composition.

basis: Three structures share this host. SrPrCoO4 and Pr0.75Sr1.25CoO4 are n=1 K2NiF4 Ruddlesden-Popper, which is the seed hypothesis and holds for them -- the third paper is on Sr-doped two-dimensional cobaltites. Pr1-xSrxCoO3 at x = 0.3-0.5 (7 samples) is the plain GdFeO3-distorted perovskite of the R1-xAxCoO3 transport paper. PrBa0.42Sr0.5Co2O5 is the A-site-ordered 112 double perovskite. The split is by the A:B ratio, 2:1 for the RP phase against 1:1 for the perovskite, with the Ba-bearing composition separate again.
reference_disagreement: The only MP entry for the chemistry is SrPr(CoO3)2 Pc mp-1218091, a computed low-symmetry ordering at hull 0.000 with no ICSD backing. It is neither the K2NiF4 phase nor the cubic perovskite, so mp_id is left null and the space group recorded is the I4/mmm of the n=1 RP archetype.

dopant_roles.basis: B-site substituent across four compositions.
B-site substituent.
Pentavalent donor on the B site.

In PrBa0.42Sr0.5Co2O5 the large Ba cation is what drives the A-site layer ordering, so it is a structural component of that composition rather than a dilute dopant; it falls below 5 at.% only because the formula has nine atoms.

basis: YCoO3 with Ca or Sr on the Y site and Ni on the Co site is all 11 compositions: the orthorhombic GdFeO3-distorted perovskite, MP YCoO3 Pnma mp-691138 with 5 ICSD references, and the papers are titled for Y1-xCaxCoO3 and for Ni-doped perovskite YCoO3. The oxygen-deficient Y2Co2O5 appears in MP at hull 0.419 but no composition here is reduced enough to be it.

dopant_roles.basis: Y1-xCaxCoO3 at x = 0.01-0.1: divalent acceptor on the A site, the hole-doping variable of the third paper and what drives the Co spin-state and insulator-metal behaviour.
Same A-site acceptor role; the first paper is on Sr substitution.
B-site substituent of the second paper.

basis: Zr(Co1-xPtx)(Sb1-ySny) across x = 0.2-0.4 and y = 0.2-0.35 is ZrCoSb half-Heusler with Pt alloyed onto the Co site and Sn on the Sb site. Both papers say so in their titles -- half-Heusler phases as prospective p-type thermoelectrics, and semimetallic (Zr,Hf)CoSb half-Heusler phases -- and every one of the nine compositions is 1:1:1.
reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this five-element host, so mp_id is null; resolve ZrCoSb itself in stage 2. Pt substitution at 20-40% of the Co site is well past a dilute limit, so the alloy may not resolve to a single MP entry at all.
note: No element in this host falls below the 5 at.% split, so there are no dopant_roles to record: Pt and Sn are both alloying levels on their respective sites and are part of the host string.

basis: LaCuSO, and LaCu1-xSO down to x = 0.075, is the whole host: the ZrCuSiAs-type oxysulfide of alternating La2O2 and Cu2S2 layers, P4/nmm, MP mp-6088 with 4 ICSD references at hull 0.000. The third paper calls it a layered oxysulfide and the first two treat it as a wide-gap p-type semiconductor, which is this structure exactly.

dopant_roles.basis: La0.925Sr0.075CuSO: divalent acceptor in the La2O2 layer, the hole-doping knob of this family and the co-doping partner in the second paper.
Same acceptor role on the La site.
LaCu0.925Mn0.075SO -- the second paper is on Sr and Mn co-doped LaCuSO as a dilute magnetic semiconductor, so Mn sits in the Cu2S2 layer.
Transition metal on the Cu site of the same layer.

note: LaCu0.97SO through LaCu0.99SO are copper vacancies, not a foreign element: the first paper is on the effect of Cu off-stoichiometry, so stage 3 should treat that deficiency as the carrier-concentration variable (non-stoichiometry) even though Cu is above the 5% cut and carries no dopant_roles entry.

basis: Pr1.85Ce0.15CuO4 is 9 of the 19 samples and Pr2CuO4 with Zn on the Cu site is most of the rest: the n=1 K2NiF4 stoichiometry in its T-prime variant, where the apical oxygen moves into a fluorite-like layer, which is what makes this the electron-doped cuprate. The taxonomy entry states that Nd2CuO4 and Pr2CuO4 are the T-prime variant under this same id, so the seed is confirmed and the variant recorded here rather than given a new prototype. MP Pr2CuO4 I4/mmm mp-4181 carries 12 ICSD references at hull 0.000.

dopant_roles.basis: Pr2-xCexCuO4 at x = 0.15 is the electron-doping variable of the whole T-prime family and the reason these samples superconduct; it is never an impurity. Stage 3 should treat it like Sr-for-La in La2CuO4.
Pr2Cu1-xZnxO4 at x = 0.001-0.01: in-plane substitution on the CuO2 sheet, used as a pair-breaking impurity rather than a carrier dopant.
Gd1.85-xPrxCe0.15CuO4 from the second paper: another rare earth on the same A site, isostructural.

basis: GaSb with Zn on the Ga site is the base of the host -- zincblende F-43m, MP mp-1156 with 15 ICSD references at hull 0.000 -- and the (GaSb)3(1-x)(Ga2Te3)x compositions stay in the same lattice: Ga2Te3 is itself a defect zincblende and the second paper calls them Ga2Te3-GaSb vacancy compounds, so Te enters the anion site with compensating cation vacancies rather than forming a second structure. (GaSb)89.92(FeGa1.3)10.08 is the exception, a deliberate FeGa1.3 second phase in a GaSb matrix.

other_polymorphs.note: One ICSD reference at hull 0.015: the nanowire polytype of GaSb, not a phase reached by heating.

dopant_roles.basis: Ga1-xZnxSb at x = 0.001-0.01, the acceptor of the first paper (Thermoelectric properties of Zn-doped GaSb).

Introduced as Ga2Te3 rather than as dilute Te: the composition sits on the GaSb-Ga2Te3 vacancy-compound line, so it brings cation vacancies with it and is an end member below 5 at.%, not a simple donor.
(GaSb)89.92(FeGa1.3)10.08: FeGa1.3 is a separate intermetallic phase dispersed in the matrix, the nanostructuring approach of the third paper.

basis: PdHx from x = 0.47 to 0.94 with dilute Ce or Ge in the metal lattice, all from one paper on the thermopower of hydrogenated palladium and its dilute alloys. Hydrogen occupies the octahedral interstices of the fcc Pd lattice, MP HPd Fm-3m mp-24289 at hull 0.000, and x is the doping variable this entry describes.

dopant_roles.basis: Pd0.97Ce0.03H0.5: a dilute substitutional impurity in the fcc metal, the dilute-alloy half of the paper.
Pd0.95Ge0.05H, same substitutional role in the metal lattice.

note: The curator details record the alpha and alpha-plus-beta hydride fields (0.25 < c < 0.6), which is a miscibility gap between two fcc phases of different H content. That is a two-phase field of one prototype, not a change of structure, so it is noted rather than recorded as a transition. H3Pd4 R-3m mp-1224413 in the reference line is an ordered hydrogen superstructure of the same fcc metal sublattice.

basis: Y2-xBixIr2O7 at x = 0-0.4 is the whole host: the A2B2O7 pyrochlore iridate, Fd-3m, MP Y2Ir2O7 mp-1191749 at hull 0.000, and the third paper names the pyrochlore iridate Y2Ir2O7 in its title while the first is on Y2-xBixIr2O7 directly.

dopant_roles.basis: Y2-xBixIr2O7 up to x = 0.4: a lone-pair cation on the A site, which widens the Ir-O-Ir angle and drives the metal-insulator behaviour. At that level it is alloying rather than dilute doping.
Transition metal on the B site of the pyrochlore.

basis: UN is 14 of the 19 samples and is the rocksalt mononitride the seed names, MP Fm-3m mp-1865 with 25 ICSD references at hull 0.000; the (GdN)5-10(UN)90-95 films are the same structure since GdN is also rocksalt. U2N3 is not: the sesquinitride is the bixbyite-type Mn2O3 structure in its alpha form, and the first paper is titled Uranium Nitride U2N3 as a novel thermoelectric material, so the host holds two prototypes and splits on the N:U ratio.
reference_disagreement: MP places U2N3 at P-3m1 mp-973 with 6 ICSD references, which is the beta (La2O3-type) sesquinitride, while the alpha form usually met on heating UN in nitrogen is cubic bixbyite Ia-3. No Ia-3 entry appears in the reference line, so the bixbyite call here rests on the nitride literature rather than on the references, and which form the paper made is unresolved. Recording it as bixbyite rather than following MP is deliberate.

dopant_roles.basis: (GdN)5.07(UN)94.93 and (GdN)9.97(UN)90.03: GdN is isostructural rocksalt, so this is a (U,Gd)N solid solution -- a burnable-poison composition in the fuel literature -- rather than dilute doping.

note: The measured range reaches 1981 K (full span 2596 K), by far the highest in this chunk, which is consistent with nuclear-fuel property measurements rather than thermoelectric ones. UN melts near 3100 K and does not change structure below it, so no transition is recorded for the rocksalt phase.

basis: The 47-oxygen phases Nb8W9O47, Nb5W12O47 and Nb4W13O47 are 10 of the 19 samples and are tetragonal tungsten bronzes -- the second paper is titled Tetragonal tungsten bronzes Nb8-xW9+xO47-delta, and the taxonomy already lists Nb5W12O47 and Nb4W13O47 as representative materials of the tungsten_bronze entry. The seed hypothesis is still right for the rest: the (W1.083O3)x(Nb2.1O5)1-x mixtures at x = 0.31 and 0.48 work out to W:Nb near 0.23 and 0.48, far on the Nb-rich side of the 47 series, which is the Wadsley-Roth block-structure region. So the host holds both and splits on the W:Nb ratio.
taxonomy_feedback: The same 47-oxygen series sits in two entries: block_shear_niobate names Nb8W9O47 in its notes while tungsten_bronze lists Nb5W12O47 and Nb4W13O47 in representative_materials. They are tetragonal tungsten bronzes and belong in tungsten_bronze; block_shear_niobate should keep Nb12O29, Nb12WO33 and the Nb-rich Wadsley-Roth phases. Worth fixing before v4, since this host is the only place both entries are cited.
reference_disagreement: MP has Nb12WO33 C2 mp-1198790 (1 ICSD reference, hull 0.041) and NbWO7 Ima2 at hull 0.376 -- a block phase and a computed one. Neither is a 47-oxygen bronze, so no mp_id is recorded for either prototype here, and the TTB symmetry variant is left unresolved rather than guessed.
note: The delta in Nb8-xW9+xO47-delta is oxygen deficiency from the reduced single-step synthesis of the first paper, i.e. the carrier-concentration variable. No element in this host falls below the 5 at.% split, so there are no dopant_roles.

basis: The host is the Ag2Te-Ag2S pseudobinary: Ag4TeS is Ag2Te plus Ag2S in equal parts, and Ag2Te0.8S0.2 and Ag2Te0.6S0.4 are S-substituted silver telluride. The low-temperature structure is the monoclinic P2_1/c hessite/acanthite type rather than the orthorhombic naumannite the entry is named for -- the taxonomy notes that difference and keeps them in one shard -- and the 297-723 K window crosses the superionic transition of both end members, above which the cation sublattice is disordered on a bcc/fcc anion frame. The seed is refined for a second reason as well: the two papers describe Ag4TeS as a ductile amorphous/crystalline composite and as a semiconductor glass, so for 13 of the 18 samples a crystalline prototype describes only part of the material.

solid_solution_axis.note: S/(S+Te) spans 0.20-0.50 over 12 compositions, i.e. the whole Ag2Te-Ag2S join up to the 1:1 Ag4TeS point. The transition temperature moves along it -- Ag2Te transforms near 418 K and Ag2S near 452 K -- so the single value recorded in phases cannot cover the host and is flagged as approximate.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: S and Te are the same group on the same anion sublattice.

reference_disagreement: The taxonomy gives 406 K for this transition, which is the Ag2Se value; this host contains no Ag2Se, so 418 K (Ag2Te) is used instead and the basis is recorded as llm_materials_knowledge rather than taxonomy_default. MP offers only Ag2TeS3 Cc mp-29163, a thio-tellurite of different stoichiometry, so mp_id is null throughout.

basis: LaAl2 and its dilute-Ce variants are 12 of the 18 samples: the cubic C15 Laves phase, MP LaAl2 Fd-3m mp-2694 with 15 ICSD references at hull 0.000, and the first paper is titled Thermoelectric power of RAl2. The (La,Ce)Al3 compositions are a different structure -- MP puts LaAl3 at P6_3/mmc mp-959 with 4 ICSD references, the hexagonal Ni3Sn D0_19 type -- and the taxonomy has only the cubic L1_2 entry for AB3, so ni3sn_d019 is proposed before use and the host splits on the Al:La ratio.

dopant_roles.basis: (La1-xCex)Al2 at x = 0.006-0.015 and Ce0.01-0.1La0.9-0.99Al3. Dilute Ce is the single-ion Kondo impurity whose giant thermopower these three papers measure -- the second is titled Giant thermoelectric power of (La,Ce)Al2 -- so it is a magnetic impurity on the rare-earth site, not a carrier dopant.

basis: RuAl2 with Fe, Si, Mn or a rare earth substituted into it is the whole host, and RuAl2 is the semiconducting TiSi2 (C54) intermetallic: MP Al2Ru Fddd (70) mp-10910 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, the same orthorhombic C54 structure proposed as tisi2_c54 for RuGa2 in chunk 005. The second paper is titled for binary semiconducting intermetallic compounds, which is what this narrow-gap Fddd aluminide is. Al13Ru4 and Al3Ru2 exist in the chemistry but no composition here is near their stoichiometries.

dopant_roles.basis: Ru0.85Fe0.15Al2 and (Ru0.85Fe0.15)0.95-0.98Mn0.02-0.05Al2: 15% of the Ru site is an alloying level, not dilute doping, and it is the base composition the Mn and Si series are built on.
Ru0.85Fe0.15Al1.95Si0.05; the first paper is on silicon- and manganese-doped RuAl2, so Si is the main-group substituent on the Al site.
The other dopant of that paper, on the transition-metal site.

Rare-earth additions to RuAl2 appear in three compositions, but nothing in the composition strings says whether they substitute on a lattice site or form a rare-earth aluminide second phase, and the rare earths are far too large for either site. Left unknown rather than assumed.
Same as Ce: addition of unresolved role.
Same as Ce: addition of unresolved role.

basis: PrBaCo2O5+delta -- Pr0.94BaCo2O5, Pr0.94BaCo2O6, PrBaCo2O5 and the Ca-substituted variants -- is the A-site-ordered 112 double perovskite of the two fuel-cell cathode papers, so the seed holds for those compositions. Pr0.5Ba0.5CoO3 and Pr0.7Ba0.3CoO3 are the disordered simple perovskite of the R1-xAxCoO3 transport paper: the same cations without the layer ordering. As in the La analogue, the cation ratio cannot tell them apart -- the oxygen content and the A-site ordering do -- so the host is mixed and the split rule has to use oxygen.

dopant_roles.basis: PrBa0.42Sr0.5Co2O5 and relatives: isovalent alkaline earth on the ordered A site, used to tune the tolerance factor. At half the Ba site it is alloying rather than doping.
Pr0.9Ca0.1BaCo2O5 -- the third paper is titled for A-site calcium-doped Pr1-xCaxBaCo2O5+delta, so Ca sits on the rare-earth half of the ordered A site.

basis: (Sr,Ba)PbO3 across Ba/(Ba+Sr) = 0.3-0.5 is an ABO3 perovskite with tetravalent Pb on the B site -- the papers are titled for perovskite-type Sr1-xBaxPbO3 ceramics and for A-site doped (Sr0.6Ba0.4)1-xMx perovskites. Ba0.4Sr0.6Pb1.1-1.2O3.2-3.4 is the same phase prepared with excess PbO, which is a processing surplus rather than a second structure.

solid_solution_axis.note: Ba/(Ba+Sr) spans 0.30-0.50 over 17 compositions. Both end members are ABO3 perovskites so the prototype is constant; the substitution moves the tolerance factor and hence the octahedral tilt, which is why the space group is given as the orthorhombic tilt system with medium confidence rather than cubic.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Ba and Sr are the same group on the same 12-coordinate site.

reference_disagreement: MP offers only BaSr(PbO3)2 Pmc2_1 mp-1227843, a computed 1:1 A-site ordering at hull 0.007. These samples scan x continuously and are a disordered solid solution, so the ordered cell is not their structure and mp_id is left null.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi goes on the B site in this family -- BaPb1-xBixO3 is the classic bismuthate line -- not on the A site with Ba and Sr, which is the natural but wrong reading of an A-site doping paper title.
Trivalent donor on the A site; the third paper is on A-site doped (Sr0.6Ba0.4)1-xMxPbO3.

basis: Every composition is Bi2Te3 with a carbon addition (Bi2Te3Cx at x = 0.3-3) and the curator details name graphene/Bi2Te3, CNT/Bi2Te3 and vol% additions of 2 to 20. That is a matrix plus a second phase, not a carbide and not a solid solution: carbon takes no lattice site in Bi2Te3. The matrix itself is tetradymite, recorded as the alternative so stage 2 resolves the Bi2Te3 structure rather than treating the host as structureless.
note: Carbon is above the 5 at.% split in every composition here -- Bi2Te3C3 is a third carbon by atom count -- so it appears as a host element and carries no dopant_roles entry, even though it is physically a dispersed second phase. The Bi2(Se,Te)3 composite of the third paper adds Se to the matrix, but no Se composition is visible in the shown subset.

basis: YbCd2-xZnxSb2 across the whole Cd/(Cd+Zn) range is the CaAl2Si2-type trigonal Zintl phase: Yb between [M2Sb2] slabs of edge-sharing MSb4 tetrahedra, P-3m1. The first paper is titled for the Zintl phase YbCd2-xZnxSb2 and the second surveys AM2Sb2 (A = Ca, Sr, Ba, Eu, Yb; M = Zn, Cd) as one structural family, so both end members are the same prototype and the solid solution never leaves it.

solid_solution_axis.note: Cd/(Cd+Zn) spans 0.20-0.85 over 15 compositions, which is the whole YbZn2Sb2-YbCd2Sb2 join. Isostructural end members, so the prototype is constant and the mixing acts on mass contrast and band width.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Cd and Zn are the same group on the same tetrahedral site.

reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this four-element host. mp_id is left null; stage 2 should resolve YbCd2Sb2 and YbZn2Sb2 separately.

basis: NaCo2-xFexO4 from x = 0.4 to 1.4 is the gamma-NaxCoO2 layered cobaltite written in its historic NaCo2O4 form: edge-sharing (Co,Fe)O2 sheets with Na between them at Na:(Co+Fe) = 1:2, which is Na0.5MO2. Two of the four papers are titled for NaCo2-xFexOy. Confidence is medium rather than high because the Fe-rich end (NaCo0.6Fe1.4O4) is past the point where the gamma stacking is usually retained, and the third paper is on Na0.7CoO2, so the Na content itself varies between papers more than the strings suggest.
reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this chemistry, so mp_id is null and the P6_3/mmc space group is the family archetype rather than a measured one.
note: Fe is above the 5 at.% split in every composition and so carries no dopant_roles entry, but its role is clear from the stoichiometry: it substitutes for Co inside the MO2 sheet across the whole series. alpha-NaFeO2 (the ordered-rocksalt 1:1 phase, alpha_nafeo2_layered) is the neighbouring structure in this chemistry, but no composition here reaches Na:M = 1:1.

basis: Nickel with 5 to 31 at.% chromium is the nichrome fcc substitutional solid solution -- Cr is soluble in fcc Ni to roughly 35 at.% and no composition here exceeds that, Ni68.6Cr31.4 being the extreme. The papers are on metallic thermocouple alloys and on hydrogen dissolved in nickel-chromium alloys, which is the interstitial-H version of the same fcc lattice rather than a different phase.
reference_disagreement: Every MP entry for this chemistry is an ordered compound -- Cr3Ni Pm-3m at hull 0.148, CrNi3 I4/mmm, Cr2Ni and CrNi2 Fd-3m at hulls of 0.21-0.27 -- each with a single ICSD reference, and MP flags CrNi3 ambiguous. None of them is the disordered fcc alloy these samples are, so mp_id is left null rather than taking the nearest formula. This is the standard failure mode of matching a random solid solution against a database of line compounds.

basis: Cu2GeSe3 with In or Sb on the Ge site, plus slightly Cu- and Se-deficient variants, is all 16 compositions. MP Cu2GeSe3 Imm2 mp-4728 (2 ICSD references, hull 0.000) is the orthorhombic ordered-zincblende structure this entry names, and the third paper calls the family ternary diamondlike semiconductors.

other_polymorphs.note: Cc at hull 0.002 with one ICSD reference, and a further Fdd2 entry mp-1225866 at hull 0.004. These are cation-ordering variants of the same diamond-like net at essentially the same energy; the first paper is titled for crystallographic control at the nanoscale, so which ordering forms is synthesis-dependent rather than reached by heating.

dopant_roles.basis: Cu2Ge1-xInxSe3 at x = 0.05-0.15, the subject of the second paper: a trivalent cation on the tetravalent Ge site, so it is an acceptor.
Same cation site; single composition.

basis: The visible compositions are Cux(TiO2)1-x at x = 18-46 at.%, which is Cu powder added to reduced TiO2-x -- a metal/oxide composite, the first paper being on the effect of Cu powder addition to Cu/TiO2-x. That confirms the seed for those. But the dopant-candidate list (Ru 7, Y 5, Ca 4, Cr 4, Mn 4 and six single rare earths) cannot come from a Cu/TiO2 composite: it is the signature of CaCu3Ti4O12, where Ca is exactly 5 at.% of the 20-atom formula and Ru, Cr and Mn substitute on the Ti site while rare earths go on the Ca site. The second paper, on complex transition-metal oxides, fits that reading. So the host mixes a Cu/TiO2 composite with the CCTO family and needs a per-composition split. Only 6 of its 18 compositions are shown in the chunk file, so the proportion between the two cannot be settled here.
reference_disagreement: The MP entries offered are Ti3Cu3O and Ti4Cu2O Fd-3m suboxides and two rare-earth cuprotitanates; none is either a Cu/TiO2 composite or CaCu3Ti4O12, so mp_id is null. The rare-earth Ti-Cu-O entries do at least corroborate that rare earths and Ti-Cu-O coexist in real structures.

dopant_roles.basis: If the unseen compositions are CaCu3Ti4O12, Ca is the A-site cation of that structure -- a host constituent, listed as a candidate only because 1 atom in 20 is exactly at the 5% cut -- not a dopant. Recorded as unknown because the composition strings that would settle it are not shown.
Ru appears in 7 compositions, which in this chemistry is the CaCu3Ti4-xRuxO12 series; Ru would sit on the octahedral Ti site.
Same octahedral B site; the third paper is on a YCr0.5Mn0.5O3-type oxide, so Cr and Mn arrive together.
Same octahedral B site as Cr.

basis: Gd1-xSrxMnO3 at x = 0.3-0.7 is all five compositions, and two of the three papers are titled for Gd-Sr manganites and for Gd1-xSrxMnO3. Gd is a small A cation so the tolerance factor is low and the GdFeO3-type octahedral tilt large, but nothing leaves the ABO3 line, so one prototype covers the host.

The third paper reports structural distortion as the variable behind the thermoelectric behaviour, which is exactly what a reference would be needed to pin down.

basis: Ge0.5Sn0.25Pb0.25Te is 7 of the 18 samples and is a GeTe-rich pseudoternary rocksalt alloy: at half GeTe the rhombohedral R3m distortion survives at room temperature and relaxes to cubic Fm-3m on heating, which is what the first and third papers are about (phase morphology in Pb0.25Sn0.25Ge0.5Te, and band inversion giving multiple valleys). Sn0.8Ge0.1Pb0.1Te is the opposite end of the same join and is cubic rocksalt throughout, so the host holds both prototypes and splits on the Ge fraction.

solid_solution_axis.note: Ge/(Ge+Sn) spans 0.11-0.86 over 12 compositions, but Pb occupies the same cation site as well, so the real axis is a three-way cation mixture. The rhombohedral-to-cubic boundary moves along it, which is why the transition temperature is recorded as composition-dependent rather than as a host constant.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Ge, Sn and Pb are all group 14 on the same cation site.

note: The chunk file shows no MEASUREMENT CROSSES A TRANSITION line for this host because no single prototype was hypothesised for it, so the transition is added here from the chemistry: pure GeTe transforms near 700 K and alloying with 50% PbTe plus SnTe lowers it substantially. 600 K is an estimate for the dominant composition and needs a paper to confirm, which is why transition_basis is llm_materials_knowledge and both phases are medium confidence.

Ge0.5Sn0.25Pb0.25TeAg0.003, a monovalent acceptor on the cation site.
Ge0.5Sn0.25Pb0.25Te1.0009Bi0.0006, a trivalent donor on the cation site.

basis: Every composition is MPt4Ge12 with M = Pr, Ce, La, Eu or Th: the germanide filled skutterudite, a Pt4Ge12 framework of Ge12 cages in Im-3 with the guest inside. That is the RyM4X12 archetype of this entry with X = Ge rather than Sb or P, and all three papers are on PrPt4Ge12 and its La/Ce/Eu/Th-substituted relatives. The framework never changes across the 18 compositions; only the guest does.

dopant_roles.basis: The guest in the Ge12 cage of PrPt4Ge12. The fillers fall below 5 at.% only because one guest serves sixteen framework atoms, and mixing two guests halves each fraction again -- they are the compound, not impurities in it.
Pr1-xCexPt4Ge12: Ce substitutes for Pr on the cage site, which is what the first paper probes.
La1-xMxPt4Ge12 of the third paper; same cage site.
Pr0.5Eu0.5Pt4Ge12; same cage site.
Tetravalent actinide guest in the same cage, used to change the electron count without a 4f moment.

basis: LaS1.33-1.50 is the gamma-La3-xS4 phase: a cubic I-43d Th3P4 framework whose La vacancies run continuously from metallic La3S4 to semiconducting La2S3, which is exactly the carrier-concentration knob this entry describes. dopant_roles.basis: La2Ti0.075S2.67, from the paper on lanthanum sesquisulfide with Ti additive. Ti is added as a sintering and grain-control additive; nothing says it enters the La site, and it is too small for it.
Divalent cation on the La site, which fills vacancies and lowers the carrier count.
Divalent rare earth on the La site of the Th3P4 framework.

basis: SrMoO3 with Mg, Fe, Co or Al on the Mo site is the whole host: the reduced Mo4+ cubic perovskite, MP SrMoO3 Pm-3m mp-18747 with 5 ICSD references. SrMo0.9Fe0.1O3 and SrMo0.8Fe0.2O3, B-site substitution at alloying levels.
SrMo0.9Co0.1O3-delta is the third paper title exactly.
Trivalent cation on the same B site.
Rare earth on the A site; appears in 5 compositions, in the SOFC anode series.

(Nb1-xTix)4SiTe4 at x = 0.002-0.05 -- one d electron fewer, so this is the hole doping of the first paper title.
Pnictogen on the chalcogen sheath site; single composition.

La0.2Sr0.8VO3: trivalent donor on the A site, which is how this family is driven across the Mott transition.

basis: PbSnTeSe in equal parts is the four-component rocksalt solid solution the papers call a high-entropy alloy: Pb and Sn share the cation site, Te and Se the anion site, and every end member of the join is Fm-3m rocksalt. The structure prototype is therefore rocksalt, with high_entropy_alloy recorded alongside as the disorder descriptor rather than as the structure -- the papers are titled for PbSnTeSe high-entropy alloys and for Na-doped nanocrystalline PbSnTeSe.

solid_solution_axis.note: Pb/(Pb+Sn) spans 0.20-0.89 over 17 compositions, and Te/Se mix independently on the anion site, so this host is disordered on both sublattices at once. That is what the high-entropy label is describing; the prototype does not change along either axis.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Pb and Sn are the same group on the cation site; Te and Se likewise on the anion site.

reference_disagreement: MP offers SnTePbSe R3m mp-1218892 (hull 0.024) and P4/mmm mp-1218887, both computed orderings of the four species. The samples are a disordered solid solution, not an ordered cell, so mp_id is left null. A computed low-symmetry ordering is the standard artefact for a high-entropy composition in a database of ordered structures.

dopant_roles.basis: Pb1-xSnTeSeLax at x = 0.02-0.1: a trivalent donor on the cation site.

basis: Both halves of the seed are present and a third thing besides. Te95Se5 and the (Bi2Se3)x(Te3)y compositions are trigonal Te with Se substituting on the helical chains -- Se and Te form a continuous trigonal solid solution -- and the first paper is on the effect of selenium on the thermoelectric properties of tellurium. (Te85Se15)45As35Cu25 is the Te-As-Cu chalcogenide glass of the second paper, which is the amorphous half. The rest are that glass with 10-50% Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 added, i.e. tetradymite crystallites in a glass matrix, which is a composite and is recorded as one rather than being forced into either half.

solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) spans 0.05-0.29 with a median of 0.09, so this is Te with a little Se rather than a balanced alloy. Trigonal Se and Te are isostructural, so the prototype holds across the axis -- but the axis is only meaningful for the crystalline compositions; in the glass compositions Se is a network component with no site at all.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Se and Te are the same group and both form the same helical chain structure.

reference_disagreement: MP offers only Te3Se P6_3/mmc mp-1187404 at hull 0.200, a computed ordering that is not the trigonal chain structure of either element. mp_id is null.

dopant_roles.basis: As is 35 at.% of the (Te85Se15)45As35Cu25 glass, i.e. a network former of the chalcogenide glass, not a dopant. It falls under the 5% cut only after dilution by the Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 additions.
Cu is 25 at.% of the same glass; as for As, it is a glass constituent.
A further glass-former constituent in the Te-based glass-ceramic compositions.
Sb arrives entirely as the Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 crystallites added to the glass, so it belongs to a second phase rather than substituting in trigonal Te.
As Sb: from the added Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 and from Bi2Se3 in the third paper, both second phases in a Te matrix.

basis: AgInSe2 with Zn on either cation site is the chalcopyrite the seed names -- TEDesignLab gives InAgSe2 I-42d mp-20554 with 13 ICSD references at hull 0.000, the best-attested entry in the chemistry. But the single largest composition is AgIn5Se8 (5 samples), and that is not chalcopyrite: it is the In-rich ordered-vacancy compound, which TEDesignLab itself lists at space group 111 rather than 122. The two are different prototypes, so defect_chalcopyrite_ovc is proposed before use and the host splits on the In:Ag ratio.
reference_disagreement: The two references disagree about AgIn5Se8: TEDesignLab gives space group 111 while MP gives In5AgSe8 C2 (5) mp-1224092 at hull 0.003. Following the project precedence the ICSD-backed TEDesignLab symmetry is preferred, but neither is confirmed here and the ordered-vacancy compounds of this family are known to take several closely related tetragonal orderings. MP also lists three further AgInSe2 polymorphs (R-3m, R3m, I4_1/amd) at hulls of 0.07-0.11, none of them the ambient chalcopyrite.

dopant_roles.basis: The second paper is titled for the site occupations of Zn in AgInSe2-based chalcopyrites, and the composition strings show the answer is not single-valued: Ag0.95InZn0.05Se2 puts Zn on the Ag site while Ag0.975In0.975Zn0.05Se2 splits it between both cation sites. The site is composition-dependent and stage 2 should keep both.
Divalent cation on the cation sublattice, as for Zn.

basis: In0.53Ga0.47As and In0.52Al0.48As lattice-matched to InP, grown as films, superlattices, devices and modules -- all zincblende III-V. Er is not a dopant here: ErAs is a semimetallic rocksalt second phase deliberately embedded as nanoparticles, and the curator details say so directly (0.6 vol% ErAs, 0.6 at.% ErAs, ErAs nanoparticles inside In0.53Ga0.27Al0.20As), which is what all three papers are built on.

solid_solution_axis.note: Al/(Al+Ga) spans 0.20-0.51 over 10 compositions, but In sits on the same site and is the majority cation, so the detected axis is only the Al/Ga part of a three-way III-site mixture held at the InP lattice constant. The composition is set by lattice matching, not by a doping series.
solid_solution_axis.axis_check: Al, Ga and In are all group 13 on the same cation site.

reference_disagreement: No reference line is offered for this four-element host, so mp_id is null. Stage 2 should resolve InAs, GaAs and AlAs separately rather than looking for one entry for the quaternary.

dopant_roles.basis: ErAs nanoparticles embedded in the InGaAlAs matrix at 0.3-0.6%: a rocksalt semimetal second phase used for electron filtering and phonon scattering, not a substitutional rare earth. Deliberate rather than a contaminant, but it is not in the zincblende lattice.
